## Motivation

`MambaComponent._alloc_mamba_slot` hard-asserted (`AssertionError: Can not
alloc mamba cache`) whenever the mamba pool was exhausted AND eviction could
not reclaim a slot. This is not a memory-budget bug: under concurrency every

title: Run warmup forward pass before memory profiling
body:
## Summary

On first launch, JIT-compiled kernel code (FlashInfer, custom ops) is generated during the profiling forward pass inside `memory_profiling()`. This compiled code lives in GPU memory permanently at the CUDA driver level — it is **not** freed by `torch.empty_cache()`.

When compilation happens inside the `memory_profiling` context, it inflates `non_torch_increase`, which shrinks the KV-cache budget. A second run (restart) doesn't suffer because the kernel cache is already warm.

This was observed on **SM120 (RTX 5090)** with NVFP4 KV cache, where FlashInfer JIT compilation is particularly heavy:
- NVFP4 paged KV kernels (swizzle_v_sf layout)
- VO-split prefill kernels (two-pass 256 for head_dim=512)

title: Fix prefill batch iter logging under overlap
body:
## Summary
- bind a stable forward_iter to each launched prefill batch
- preserve that batch-local iter when the batch snapshot is copied into the result queue
- log Prefill batch using the batch's own iter instead of the current global forward_ct

## Why
Under overlap scheduling, the scheduler can launch the current batch before processing the previous batch result and increase forward_ct. The old prefill logging used the current global forward_ct when emitting Prefill batch lines, so completed batches could be mislabeled as a later iter.
When next iter has nothing to launch and didn't increase forward_ct, consecutive completed batches could even be printed with the same iter id.

body:
## Motivation

HiCache currently uses a single auxiliary I/O worker per controller to consume `prefetch_buffer` and execute storage-to-host `_page_transfer()` operations.

Under bursty long-context workloads, multiple prefetch operations can finish the storage hit query and TP synchronization within a short period, but their actual storage reads are still serialized by that single worker. title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Honor leading strides in SM120 blockwise FP8 GEMM
body:
## Purpose

`scaled_mm_blockwise_sm120_fp8_dispatch.cuh` builds A/B/C strides with `make_cute_packed_stride` from the logical shape, so a padded view such as `(8, 256)` with stride `(384, 1)` is read with row stride 256. Pass `a.stride(0)`, `b.stride(1)` and `out.stride(0)` through instead. With `swap_ab` (`M <= 64` here) the output is the column-major transpose, so its leading stride goes in component 1.
